story.originalTitle: Why Honda's F1 project looks completely different from its Red Bull years
story.summaryEn: Honda chief engineer Shintaro Orihara says Honda's philosophy is "unique", with staff and knowledge constantly rotating between road car projects and F1. Adrian Newey spoke openly about Honda's battery problems at the FIA team principals' press conference in Melbourne.
detailZh: 为什么本田的F1项目看起来与它的红牛时代完全不同
总工程师Shintaro Orihara表示，本田的理念是“独特的”，员工和知识在公路车项目与F1之间不断轮换
当Adrian Newey在墨尔本举行的F1赛季揭幕战期间出现在FIA车队负责人新闻发布会上时，这位传奇设计师因多个原因吸引了关注。
Newey公开谈论了本田的电池问题，承认他作为车队负责人的角色在一定程度上让他从设计职责中分心，并有些夸张地说，本田在这期间主要忙于太阳能电池板。
然而，可以说最有趣的言论还在后头。那就是有消息透露，阿斯顿·马丁的领导层直到2025年11月才发现，本田F1车队的人员构成与其在红牛时期的辉煌岁月完全不同。
这件事直到2025年11月才变得清晰，听起来仍然很奇怪，毕竟协议早在2023年就已经达成。这说明了阿斯顿·马丁做了——或者没做——多少功课？难道车队在几年前签约时并不清楚自己到底要加入的是什么吗？
尽管这引发了人们对阿斯顿·马丁做法的质疑，但从本田方面来看有一个合乎逻辑的解释。赛道总经理兼首席工程师Shintaro Orihara表示，这与这家日本制造商的整体理念密切相关。
“本田是一家非常独特的公司。所以，总是，怎么说呢，员工会在公路车项目和F1项目之间流动，”Orihara告诉Autosport。
"去年，我们有很多——不是新人，而是从公路车项目转来的一些极具天赋的人，还有一些曾在红牛项目中工作过的人。
Shintaro Orihara，本田赛车公司赛道总经理兼首席工程师
"我们一直在我们的F1项目中培养人才，以提升本田的知识水平。"
其理念是让整个公司从F1中获得的知识中受益，尽管以新人员为主来建设项目也带来了显著的弊端。
在最初的开发阶段，具体的F1经验有所欠缺，而根据折原的说法，本田最终得出了完全相同的结论。
这位日本人认为：“大概在去年年底，我们整体的人员开发水平还不足以达到一级方程式的水平。”“然后在冬季测试中，我们经历了不少艰难时刻，但这些时刻锻炼了我们的人员。他们学到了很多关于我们需要在一级方程式中努力的方向。”
“他们已经有了足够的知识和高水平的技能，但[通过这些艰难时刻]他们获得了关于如何在一级方程式中工作的经验。”
2026年的头几个月是一段陡峭的学习曲线，经验不足的员工迅速适应了一级方程式的要求。
本田还以另一种方式采取了行动。当2025年底明确其员工队伍未达到所需水平时，折原表示，几位拥有红牛时代经验的本田员工被重新召回F1项目，目的就是快速注入额外的经验和专业知识。
通过其赞德福特升级，该升级已在匈牙利的一次拍摄日期间进行过测试，本田希望迈出第一个重要的步伐。
结合较新团队成员所获得的经验，折原相信本田的F1运营现在已达到所需水平。
这在一定程度上解释了艰难的组建阶段——尽管有多个因素发挥了作用——但也解释了为什么本田正以更大的信心展望未来。
“除此之外，我们的新人在冬季测试中获得了那些学习经验，”折原补充道。“我认为从那时起，我们在员工发展方面已经取得了良好进展。
“而现在我有信心，我们处于有利位置，能够开发出强大的动力单元以及强大的能量管理[为未来几年]。”
本田已经表示，通过其赞德福特升级，它希望在动力单元性能方面回到折原所说的“赛车领域”，然后在2027年底或2028年初再次成为F1的“顶级竞争者”。
detailEn: Why Honda's F1 project looks completely different from its Red Bull years
Chief engineer Shintaro Orihara says Honda's philosophy is "unique", with staff and knowledge constantly rotating between road car projects and F1
When Adrian Newey appeared at the FIA team principals' press conference during the Formula 1 season opener in Melbourne, the legendary designer attracted attention for several reasons.

Newey spoke openly about Honda's battery problems, acknowledged that his role as team principal had distracted him from his design duties to some extent, and said – with some exaggeration – that Honda had mainly been busy with solar panels in the intervening years.

Yet arguably the most interesting remark was still to come. That was the revelation that Aston Martin's leadership had only discovered in November 2025 that the makeup of Honda's F1 team was completely different from what it had been during its glory years with Red Bull.

The fact that this only became clear in November 2025 still sounds strange, given that the deal had already been agreed in 2023. What does that say about the homework Aston Martin had – or had not – done, and did the team not know exactly what it was signing up for years earlier?

Although that raises questions about Aston Martin’s approach, there is a logical explanation from Honda's side. General trackside manager and chief engineer Shintaro Orihara says it is closely linked to the Japanese manufacturer's overall philosophy.
"Honda is a very unique company. So, always, how to say, staff is moving between road car projects and the Formula 1 project," Orihara told Autosport.
"Last year, we had a lot of, not new people, but some highly talented people coming from road car projects and some others who had worked within the Red Bull project.
Shintaro Orihara, Trackside General Manager and Chief Engineer of Honda Racing Corporation
"We always develop talent in our Formula 1 project to boost Honda's knowledge."
The idea is for the company as a whole to benefit from the knowledge gained in F1, although building up the project with predominantly new personnel also came with significant drawbacks.
Specific F1 experience was lacking during the initial development phase, and according to Orihara, Honda eventually came to exactly that conclusion.

"Probably, at the end of last year, our total human development level was not sufficient for the Formula 1 level," the Japanese reckoned. "And then, at winter testing, we've had quite tough moments, but those moments have developed our people. They have learned a lot of things about what we need to work in Formula 1.
"They already had enough knowledge and high-level skills, but [with those difficult moments] they gained experience on how they need to work in Formula 1."
The opening months of 2026 have been a steep learning curve, with the inexperienced staff rapidly adapting to the demands of F1.

Honda has also taken action in another way. When it became clear at the end of 2025 that its workforce was not at the required level, Orihara says several Honda employees with experience from the Red Bull era were brought back into the F1 project, simply to provide a quick injection of additional experience and know-how.
With its Zandvoort upgrade, which has already been tested during a filming day in Hungary, Honda hopes to make a first significant step
Combined with the experience gained by the newer team members, Orihara believes Honda's F1 operation is now at the required level.
This partly explains the difficult build-up phase – although several factors have played a role – but also why Honda is looking to the future with greater confidence.
"Besides that, our new people got those learning experiences from winter testing," Orihara added. "I think that since then we have made good progress in terms of our staff development.
"And now I'm confident that we are in a good position to develop a strong power unit and also strong energy management [for the upcoming years]."

Honda has already indicated that with its Zandvoort upgrade it wants to return to what Orihara calls the "racing field" in terms of power unit performance, before targeting becoming a "top competitor" in F1 again by late 2027 or early 2028.

relatedItems.originalTitle: Cadillac F1 goes full Texas with new Tommy Hilfiger collection for US Grand Prix
relatedItems.summaryEn: The Cadillac Formula 1 Team and its partner Tommy Hilfiger have released a Texas-themed clothing collection ahead of the United States Grand Prix. The collection went on sale on Tuesday earlier this week.
detailZh: 凯迪拉克F1以全新汤米·希尔费格系列在美国大奖赛上尽显得克萨斯风情
凯迪拉克与汤米·希尔费格发布了一个以得克萨斯为灵感的五件式牛仔（denim）系列
瓦尔特利·博塔斯，凯迪拉克F1车队——图片由汤米·希尔费格提供
赛道之外的赛车文化。车手生活方式、时尚、旅行、设计，以及让赛车超越运动本身的故事。
凯迪拉克一级方程式车队及其合作伙伴汤米·希尔费格在奥斯汀美国大奖赛前发布了一个德克萨斯主题的服装系列，这让我们所有人都兴奋不已。
汤米·希尔费格与凯迪拉克一级方程式车队的奥斯汀系列于本周二早些时候开售。但这并不是这两个品牌第一次推出与比赛相关的产品。他们已经在同一城市系列中推出了迈阿密和墨西哥系列，并且还计划在11月推出拉斯维加斯系列。
不出意外的话，牛仔布是这些单品的核心，它们带有镀铬细节和汤米·希尔费格红白蓝配色的V形美国国旗。
男士可以购买基于经典卡车司机风格的浅色水洗牛仔夹克。女士则有一件带银色箔涂层的牛仔背心。一件T恤、一件背心和一顶牛仔帽让这个系列更加让人难以拒绝。你知道还有什么同样让人难以拒绝吗？可以看到凯迪拉克车手瓦尔特利·博塔斯在日落时分向镜头举起一顶牛仔帽，背上印有V形旗帜图案。
你还需要什么来说服你？
瓦尔特利·博塔斯，凯迪拉克F1车队——由汤米·希尔费格提供
“在我们的美国根源上增添一点乐趣”
汤米·希尔费格首席设计官李·霍尔曼表示，设计师们从该品牌最受欢迎的两件单品入手。
他说：“我们从 Tommy 衣橱中的标志性单品——牛仔夹克和白 T 恤——入手，并研究了如何以奥斯汀的城市气质为灵感对它们进行重新演绎。”
“关键在于把熟悉的单品赋予全新的视角，同时坚守我们经典美式酷感的品牌基因。”
凯迪拉克一级方程式车队首席品牌顾问卡西迪·托里斯表示，在得克萨斯州举行的这场比赛让两个品牌都有了发挥空间。
“奥斯汀让我们有机会在美国根源上玩得更尽兴一些，”托里斯说，“这是为比赛周末打造的粉丝服饰，但设计上力求在围场之外也能长久穿着。”
汤米·希尔费格是凯迪拉克的官方服装和车迷服饰合作伙伴，车手塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯——博塔斯的队友——也是该品牌的全球男装大使。奥斯汀站是美国车队本赛季继五月初迈阿密大奖赛之后的第二个主场比赛，佩雷斯期待能在离家更近的地方驾驶。
“我们距离能够与前车竞争还差大约一秒到一秒半，我认为我们现在真正需要的是一辆更强的赛车，”佩雷斯在新加坡站后表示。“其他一切都在按预期推进，我相信我们作为一个团队会达到目标。我非常期待奥斯汀和墨西哥，我们的两场主场比赛。
“奥斯汀是车队的主场，墨西哥对我而言将格外特别，在家乡观众面前比赛并迎来第300场大奖赛。那将是一个非常特别的周末。”
凯迪拉克在首个赛季仍在等待它的首个积分。
detailEn: Cadillac F1 goes full Texas with new Tommy Hilfiger collection for US Grand Prix
Cadillac and Tommy Hilfiger have unveiled a five-piece denim collection inspired by Texas
Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac F1 team - courtesy of Tommy Hilfiger
Motorsport culture beyond the track. Driver lifestyle, fashion, travel, design and the stories that make racing more than a sport.
The Cadillac Formula 1 Team and its partner Tommy Hilfiger have released a Texas-themed clothing collection ahead of the United States Grand Prix in Austin, and it's making us all kinds of excited.

The Tommy Hilfiger x Cadillac Formula 1 Team Austin collection went on sale on Tuesday earlier this week. But this isn't the first time the two brands have released something in connection with a race. They have already released Miami and Mexico collections in the same city series, and a Las Vegas drop is also planned for November.
Denim, maybe unsurprisingly, is the heart of these pieces, which carry chrome detailing and a chevron-shaped American flag in Tommy Hilfiger's red, white and blue.

Men can buy a light-wash denim jacket based on the classic trucker style. For women, there's a denim vest with a silver foil coating. A T-shirt, a tank top and a denim cap make the range even harder to say no to. And do you know what else does the same? Cadillac driver Valtteri Bottas can be seen tipping a cowboy hat to the camera at sunset, with the chevron flag design across his back.
What more do you need to persuade you?
Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac F1 team - courtesy of Tommy Hilfiger
"A little more fun with our American roots"
Lee Holman, Tommy Hilfiger's chief design officer, said the designers started with two of the brand's most popular pieces.
"We started with icons of the Tommy wardrobe – the denim jacket and the white T-shirt – and looked at how we could rework them inspired by the character of Austin," he said.
"It's about taking familiar pieces and giving them a fresh point of view, while staying grounded in our classic American cool DNA."
Cassidy Towriss, chief brand adviser for the Cadillac Formula 1 Team, said the race in Texas gave both brands room to play.
"Austin gives us a chance to have a little more fun with our American roots," Towriss said. "It's fanwear made for race weekend, but designed to live well beyond the paddock."

Tommy Hilfiger is Cadillac's official apparel and fanwear partner, with driver Sergio Perez, Bottas's team-mate, also the brand's global menswear ambassador. With the Austin race being the American team's second home race of the season after the Miami Grand Prix earlier this season in early May, Perez is looking forward to driving a little closer to home.

“We are still lacking around one to one-and-a-half seconds to be able to compete with the cars ahead, and I think what we really need now is a stronger car underneath us," Perez said following his Singapore campaign. "Everything else has been progressing as expected, and I’m confident we will get there as a team. I’m really looking forward to Austin and Mexico, our two home races.
"Austin for the team, and Mexico will be particularly special for me, racing in front of my home crowd and reaching 300 grands prix. It’s going to be a very special weekend.”
Cadillac is still waiting for its first points in its debut season.
